question: This question uses capital expenditures as a stand-in for AI infrastructure spending. Which three US-listed companies reported the most capital expenditures over their three most recent fiscal quarters reported as of November 6, 2026? Use the cash-flow statement in each company's 10-Q and 10-K filings: "purchases of property and equipment" (Microsoft calls it "additions to property and equipment" and Oracle "capital expenditures"), not counting assets acquired under finance leases. For most companies, these quarters are January–September 2026.
answer: Amazon ($175.67 billion, January–September 2026), Alphabet ($131.95 billion, January–September 2026) and Microsoft ($106.05 billion, January–September 2026: $30.88 + $35.80 + $39.37 billion).
pass_rule: Pass if the answer names Amazon, Alphabet (Google) and Microsoft as the three companies, in any order, and names no other company as one of the three. Amounts are not required. A wrong amount lowers the factual-accuracy score but does not fail the answer.

question: In 2026, Google launched Gemini Spark, xAI launched Grok Bot, Meta launched Muse, OpenAI launched dots and Anthropic launched Claude Duet, each an always-on personal AI agent. Which three of the five became available to users first, and when? Count the first date any outside user could use it. Betas and research previews count.
answer: Gemini Spark (Google; announced May 19, 2026 at I/O and rolled out to trusted testers that week), Grok Bot (xAI; August 11, 2026, beta) and Muse (Meta; September 8, 2026).
pass_rule: Pass if the answer names Gemini Spark, Grok Bot and Muse as the three, in any order, and names no other product as one of the three. Dates are not required. A date that is given must be within 7 days of the key.
